toegepas.voor: Sy is in Graad 6 en hy is in Graad 2.
toegepas.na: Sy was in Graad 6 en hy in Graad 2.
toegepas.rede_vinder: The story is told in the past tense, so the present 'is' jars; the repeated verb can also fall away.
toegepas.fout: A lone present-tense 'is' inside a past-tense narration where every other state uses 'was'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Brings one stray sentence into the story's own past tense without changing who is in which grade.

toegepas.voor: het Kobus op die gladde modder gegly
toegepas.na: het Kobus op die gladde modder uitgegly
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Uitgly' is the idiomatic Afrikaans verb for slipping and falling; 'gly' alone suggests sliding.
toegepas.fout: 'Gegly' means slid; the event is a slip that knocks the lunchbox open.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Uitgegly' is the exact Afrikaans verb for slipping, and the meaning is unchanged.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Net' for 'only just' is an English calque; Afrikaans uses 'eers' for a recent point in time.
toegepas.fout: 'Net die vorige week' copies English 'just the previous week'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Eers die vorige week' is the natural Afrikaans for a recent move and keeps the meaning.

toegepas.voor: Hy wou die volgende dag vroeër gaan om voor die klok te speel.
toegepas.na: Hy wou die volgende dag vroeër skool toe gaan om te speel voordat die klok lui.
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Vroeër gaan' lacks a destination and 'voor die klok' is elliptical; spelling both out keeps the meaning and reads naturally.
toegepas.fout: 'Vroeer gaan' has no destination and 'voor die klok te speel' is clipped and makes the reader stumble.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Spells out what is already implied, school and before the bell rings, without adding a fact.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Motorhuis' is the standard Afrikaans word; 'garage' is an informal borrowing.
toegepas.fout: 'Garage' is a borrowing that can also mean a petrol station.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Motorhuis' is the standard Afrikaans word for the same building.

toegepas.voor: Sy knieë was styf en hy moes
toegepas.na: Sy knieë was styf, en hy moes
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: 'en' joins two sentences that each have their own subject and verb, so a comma goes before it.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses each with its own subject and verb.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Sy knieë was styf' and 'hy moes ... rus' are full sentences, so the comma is required.

laat_vaar.voor: In Kobus se klas was 'n nuwe seun
laat_vaar.na: In Kobus se klas was daar 'n nuwe seun
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: An existential sentence introducing a new character reads more naturally with 'daar'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: With the place phrase fronted, the sentence already reads naturally without 'daar'; the change is lateral.

laat_vaar.na: Daardie aand het Lwazi se ma
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The new paragraph opens with 'sy' right after a sentence about the old man, so naming her makes the reference clear.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Sy' cannot point to the old man and Lwazi's mother is the subject of the previous paragraph, so the name only adds repetition.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'n Bak van haar pampoensop' copies the English 'a bowl of her soup'; Afrikaans says simply 'n bak pampoensop'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Dropping 'van haar' loses that it was her own soup, and the original is normal Afrikaans.

laat_vaar.voor: Nadia het omgekyk na die huise langs die veld.
laat_vaar.na: Nadia het na die huise langs die veld omgekyk.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The separable verb belongs at the end of the clause in standard Afrikaans word order.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Placing the prepositional phrase after the participle is accepted Afrikaans and suits the story's rhythm; the change is lateral.
